main_body: T-shaped timber: a wide horizontal beam (rows 9-17) on a narrow vertical post (rows 18-47)
top_band: light orange speckled band, rows 10-12, with a cream highlight line at row 13
evidence: Reading down the middle of the beam: dark outline at row 9, a light orange top band at rows 10-12, a cream front-edge line at row 13, then a darker orange-to-brown front face at rows 14-17 ending in a dark base line. The beam shows a real top surface with a distinct front edge and a darker face under it. The post below is a narrow vertical shaft whose top is hidden by the beam, so it needs no top face. The top band is thin but reads as a surface, and the beam is the horizontal element that must show a top face. Borderline, but it passes.

style.evidence: The outline is dark brown and tinted, which is fine. The wood has only about 4 tones, with a few speckle dots on the beam. The post is a 6px stripe with a light centre, a mid edge and a dark side, so most of its tiles carry only 3-5 colours. Next to the reference stall and well, which have many materials, tile scallops and stone shading, this reads as thin, simple and sticker-like. It is much lower in density and richness.
